first.rationale:
The competitor's entry pricing makes promotional_pricing the emotionally obvious move, but memory_73 is the one inherited claim that carries an explicit self-flagged defect: the readout pooled two cohorts after a mid-test redefinition, so its 'strong acquisition and revenue lift' may be an artifact of the pooling rather than a real effect. That is exactly the memory whose source record is worth an analyst pull, both because it is the loudest and because acting on it would be the hardest to reverse. Discount-led acquisition also carries a downstream value risk that the metric it lifts (raw acquisition/revenue) diverges from the objective (sustainable long-term qualified revenue): price-anchored SMB accounts acquired under a competitor-matching promo tend to be the lowest-retention, most churn-prone cohort, and a promo sets a price anchor that persists past the test window. Second pull is memory_86, because it is the direct evidentiary basis for my intended action and I would rather verify the memory I plan to rely on than only the one I plan to decline.

Intended action is simplify_onboarding. Two of the three current problems are onboarding completion down 4% and activation down 6%, and these are plausibly the same funnel failure observed at two points; onboarding completion is upstream of activation, so a fix there can address both, whereas activation_messaging (memory_91) treats the downstream symptom only. memory_86 and memory_31 are mutually corroborating from independent consolidations (day 52 and day 12) and both point at friction reduction in the self-serve/SMB path. Reducing onboarding friction also improves the value delivered to the price-sensitive accounts the competitor is targeting, which is a more durable defense than matching their price. referral_incentive (memory_57) targets established customers and does not address either declining metric; enterprise_sales_assist (memory_44) is credible but addresses a segment that is not the one currently bleeding.

Uncertainty I am carrying rather than resolving: all six memories are consolidated summaries of archived records, and the oldest (memory_31, day 12) is 64 days stale, so a 'durable lift' claim from then may no longer hold under current conditions. The declines could also be driven by a changed traffic mix from the competitor's launch rather than by product friction, in which case an onboarding fix would underperform. Scale is standard_experiment rather than broad_rollout: the corroboration is good enough to justify a real read but not good enough to justify committing the funnel without one. If the memory_86 pull reveals a defect comparable to memory_73's, I would drop to a small_guarded_test and reconsider activation_messaging.
